sentences.text: Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. And 3 Others Counsel for Applicant :- Kamal Dev Rai, Ajay Kumar Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A., Sudhir Kumar Singh Hon'ble Mayank Kumar Jain,J.
Supplementary affidavit filed on behalf of applicant and the counter affidavit filed on behalf of informant in Court today, are taken on record.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the entire record.

The present bail application has been filed on behalf of applicant in Case Crime No. 125 of 2022,
under Sections 363, 366, 376 I.P.C. and Section 5 J(ii)/6 of POCSO Act, Police Station Rewatipur,
District Ghazipur with the prayer to enlarge the applicant on bail.
It is submitted by learned counsel for applicant that applicant is innocent and has not committed any offence as alleged in the first information report.
The victim in her statement recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C. did not make any allegation of kidnapping against the applicant but stated that she accompanied the applicant with her own accord.
Since the applicant is a teacher, the victim fell in love with the applicant.

The victim in her statement recorded under section 164 Cr.P.C. she Indrajeet Narayan Singh vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/129628877/

sentences.text: The victim is a major.
She refused to undergo her medical examination.
No allegation of rape has been leveled against the applicant.

It is also stated that as per Bihar State School Secondary Examination, 2023 the date of birth of the victim has been mentioned as 29.11.2005 and further the victim is having pregnancy of about nine weeks.

Learned counsel for applicant lastly submits that applicant is in jail since 07.01.2023 having no criminal history and that in case applicant is enlarged on bail, applicant will not misuse the liberty of bail.

Per contra learned A.G.A. assisted by learned counsel for the informant vehemently opposed the prayer for bail and submitted that even as per documents submitted on behalf of the applicant victim is minor.
It is also submitted that the birth certificate issued by Bihar Government, the date of birth of the victim has been noted as 29.11.2008, therefore, she was minor at the time of incident.
Admittedly, the victim is minor as per high school certificate and it has been argued that presently the victim is lodged in child care home.

Considering the submissions made by learned counsel for applicant as well as learned A.G.A.,
gravity of offence and severity of punishment, I do not find any good ground to enlarge the applicant on bail.
Accordingly, the bail application of applicant, Indrajeet Narayan Singh, is hereby rejected.
However, court below is directed to record the statement of the victim positively within two months from the date of production of a certified coy of this order before it.
The applicant is directed to cooperate with the proceedings of the trial before the court below.
